questions.stem:
Heat treatment of muscular pain involves radiation of wavelength of about 900 nm. Which spectral line of H atom is suitable for this ?
Given: Rydberg constant
$R_H = 10^{5}\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$, $h = 6.6 \times 10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}$, $c = 3 \times 10^{8}\ \mathrm{m/s}$)
questions.solution:
$\lambda = 900\ \mathrm{nm} = 9 \times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{cm}$, H-atom ($Z = 1$), $R_H = 10^{5}\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$
Rydberg eq. $\frac{1}{\lambda} = R_H Z^{2} \left(\frac{1}{n_1^{2}} - \frac{1}{n_2^{2}}\right)$
$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\lambda \times R_H} = \frac{1}{n_1^{2}} - \frac{1}{n_2^{2}}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{9 \times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{cm} \times 10^{5}\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}} = \left(\frac{1}{n_1^{2}} - \frac{1}{n_2^{2}}\right)$
$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{n_1^{2}} - \frac{1}{n_2^{2}} = \frac{1}{9}$
It is possible when $n_1 = 3$, $n_2 = \infty$
Possible series : $\infty \rightarrow 3$

$\mathrm{CrCl_3 \cdot xNH_3}$ can exist as a complex. 0.1 molal aqueous solution of this complex shows a depression in freezing point of $0.558^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Assuming 100% ionisation of this complex and coordination number of Cr is 6, the complex will be
(Given $K_f = 1.86\ \mathrm{K\,kg\,mol^{-1}}$)
questions.solution:
Given : $\Delta T_f = 0.558^\circ\mathrm{C}$
$k_f = 1.86\ \frac{\mathrm{K \times kg}}{\mathrm{mol}}$
0.1 m aq. sol.
$\Rightarrow \Delta T_f = i \times k_f \times m$
$\Rightarrow 0.558 = i \times 1.86 \times 0.1$

questions.stem:
$\mathrm{FeO_4^{2-} \xrightarrow{+2.0\ V} Fe^{3+} \xrightarrow{0.8\ V} Fe^{2+} \xrightarrow{-0.5\ V} Fe^{0}}$
In the above diagram, the standard electrode potentials are given in volts (over the arrow).
The value of $E^{\Theta}_{\mathrm{FeO_4^{2-}/Fe^{2+}}}$ is
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{FeO_4^{-2} \xrightarrow[n_1=3]{E_1^\circ = 2\,V} Fe^{+3} \xrightarrow[n_2=1]{E_2^\circ = 0.8\,V} Fe^{+2} \xrightarrow{E_3^\circ = -.05\,V} Fe}$
$E_4^\circ = ?$ (from $\mathrm{FeO_4^{2-}}$ to $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$), $n_4 = 4$
$\Delta G_4^\circ = \Delta G_1^\circ + \Delta G_2^\circ$
$\Rightarrow -n_4FE_4^\circ = -n_1FE_1^\circ - n_2FE_2^\circ$
$\Rightarrow +4E_4^\circ = 3 \times 2 + (1 \times 0.8)$
$\Rightarrow E_4^\circ = \frac{6.8}{4}\ \mathrm{V}$
$\Rightarrow E_4^\circ = 1.7\ \mathrm{V}$

questions.stem:
$2.8 \times 10^{-3}$ mol of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ is left after removing $10^{21}$ molecules from its 'x' mg sample. The mass of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ taken initially is
Given : $N_A = 6.02 \times 10^{23}\ \mathrm{mol^{-1}}$
questions.solution:
$(\text{moles})_{initial} = \frac{x \times 10^{-3}}{44}$
$(\text{moles})_{removal} = \frac{10^{21}}{6.02 \times 10^{23}}$
$(\text{moles})_{left} = (\text{moles})_{initial} - (\text{moles})_{removed}$
$2.8 \times 10^{-3} = \frac{x \times 10^{-3}}{44} - \frac{10^{21}}{6.02 \times 10^{23}}$
$\Rightarrow x = 196.2\ \mathrm{mg}$

questions.stem: Ice at $-5^\circ\mathrm{C}$ is heated to become vapor with temperature of $110^\circ\mathrm{C}$ at atmospheric pressure. The entropy change associated with this process can be obtained from :
questions.solution:
Steps: (1) Ice $268\ \mathrm{K} \to 273\ \mathrm{K}$; (2) Ice $\rightleftharpoons$ Water at $273\ \mathrm{K}$; (3) Water $273\ \mathrm{K} \to 373\ \mathrm{K}$; (4) Water $\rightleftharpoons$ Water vapour at $373\ \mathrm{K}$; (5) Water vapour $373\ \mathrm{K} \to 383\ \mathrm{K}$
$\Delta S_{overall} = \Delta S_1 + \Delta S_2 + \Delta S_3 + \Delta S_4 + \Delta S_5$
$\Delta S_2 = \frac{\Delta H_{m\ fusion}}{273}$, $T_f = 273\ \mathrm{K}$
$\Delta S_3 = \int_{273}^{373} \frac{C_{p,m}\,dT}{T}$
$\Delta S_4 = \frac{\Delta H_{m\ vaporisation}}{373}$, $T_b = 373\ \mathrm{K}$
$\Delta S_5 = \int_{373}^{383} \frac{C_{p,m}\,dT}{T}$
Answer = (2)

questions.stem:
Which of the following happens when $\mathrm{NH_4OH}$ is added gradually to the solution containing 1M $\mathrm{A^{2+}}$ and 1M $\mathrm{B^{3+}}$ ions ?
Given : $K_{sp}\mathrm{[A(OH)_2]} = 9 \times 10^{-10}$ and
$K_{sp}\mathrm{[B(OH)_3]} = 27 \times 10^{-18}$ at 298 K.
questions.solution:
Condition for precipitation $Q_{ip} > K_{sp}$
For $\mathrm{[A(OH)_2]}$
$[\mathrm{A^{2+}}][\mathrm{OH^{-}}]^{2} > 9 \times 10^{-10}$
$[\mathrm{A^{+2}}] = 1\ \mathrm{M}$
$\Rightarrow [\mathrm{OH^{-}}] > 3 \times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{M}$
For $\mathrm{[B(OH)_3]}$
$[\mathrm{B^{3+}}][\mathrm{OH^{-}}]^{3} > 27 \times 10^{-18}$
$[\mathrm{B^{3+}}] = 1\mathrm{M}$
$\Rightarrow [\mathrm{OH^{-}}] > 3 \times 10^{-6}\ \mathrm{M}$
So, $\mathrm{B(OH)_3}$ will precipitate before $\mathrm{A(OH)_2}$

options.text: Both $\mathrm{A(OH)_2}$ and $\mathrm{B(OH)_3}$ do not show precipitation with $\mathrm{NH_4OH}$

questions.stem:
If 1 mM solution of ethylamine produces pH = 9, then the ionization constant ($K_b$) of ethylamine is $10^{-x}$. The value of x is ________ (nearest integer).
[The degree of ionization of ethylamine can be neglected with respect to unity.]
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{C_2H_5NH_2(aq) + H_2O \rightleftharpoons C_2H_5NH_3^{+} + OH^{-}}$
$C = 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{M}$ initially; at equilibrium: $C(1-\alpha)$, $C\alpha$, $C\alpha$
$\Rightarrow C = 10^{-3}$, $C\alpha = 10^{-5}$, $C\alpha = 10^{-5}$
$1 - \alpha \simeq 1$
Given, $pH = 9 \Rightarrow pOH = 5 \Rightarrow [\mathrm{OH^{-}}] = 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{M}$
Now, $K_b = \frac{[\mathrm{C_2H_5NH_3^{+}}][\mathrm{OH^{-}}]}{[\mathrm{C_2H_5NH_2}]}$
$\Rightarrow K_b = \frac{10^{-5} \times 10^{-5}}{10^{-3}} = 10^{-7}$

questions.stem:
For the thermal decomposition of $\mathrm{N_2O_5(g)}$ at constant volume, the following table can be formed, for the reaction mentioned below :
$\mathrm{2N_2O_5(g) \rightarrow 2N_2O_4(g) + O_2(g)}$
S.No. | Time/s | Total pressure / (atm)
1 | 0 | 0.6
2 | 100 | 'x'
$x = $ ________ $\times 10^{-3}$ atm [nearest integer]
Given : Rate constant for the reaction is $4.606 \times 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$.
questions.solution:
Sol. (ALLEN): $K_{\mathrm{N_2O_5}} = 2 \times 4.606 \times 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$
$\mathrm{2N_2O_5(g) \longrightarrow 2N_2O_4(g) + O_2(g)}$
$P_i$: 0.6, 0, 0; $P_f$: $0.6 - P$, $P$, $\frac{P}{2}$
$2 \times 4.606 \times 10^{-2} = \frac{2.303}{100}\log\frac{0.6}{0.6 - P}$
$4\log_{10}\frac{0.6}{0.6 - P}$
$10^{4} = \frac{0.6}{0.6 - P}$
$\Rightarrow 0.6 \times 10^{4} - 10^{4}P = 0.6$
$\Rightarrow 10^{4}P = 0.6(10^{4} - 1)$
$P = (6000 - 0.6) \times 10^{-4} = 5999. \times 10^{-4} = 0.59994$
$P_{Total} = 0.6 + \frac{P}{2} = 0.6 + 0.29997 = 0.89997 = 899.97 \times 10^{-3}$
Ans. 900

Given by NTA:
Given : $\mathrm{2N_2O_5(g) \rightarrow 2N_2O_4(g) + O_2(g)}$
$t = 0$: 0.6, 0, 0; $t = 100\ \mathrm{s}$: $0.6 - x$, $x$, $\frac{x}{2}$
$P_{Total} = 0.6 + \frac{x}{2}$
As given in equation $K_r = 4.606 \times 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{sec^{-1}}$
(Here language conflict in question) ($K_r = \frac{KA}{2}$ not considered)
$K_r t = \ln\frac{0.6}{0.6 - x}$
$4.606 \times 10^{-2} \times 100 = 2.303\log\frac{0.6}{0.6 - x}$
$P_{Total} = 0.6 + \frac{0.594}{2} = 0.897\ \mathrm{atm} = 897 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{atm}$

questions.stem: The standard enthalpy and standard entropy of decomposition of $\mathrm{N_2O_4}$ to $\mathrm{NO_2}$ are $55.0\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ and $175.0\ \mathrm{J/K/mol}$ respectively. The standard free energy change for this reaction at $25^\circ\mathrm{C}$ in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$ is _______ (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
$\Delta H^\circ_{rxn} = 55\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}$, $T = 298\ \mathrm{K}$
$\Delta S^\circ_{rxn} = 175\ \mathrm{J/mol}$
$\Delta G^\circ_{rxn} = \Delta H^\circ_{rxn} - T\Delta S^\circ_{rxn}$
$\Rightarrow \Delta G^\circ_{rxn} = 55000\ \mathrm{J/mol} - 298 \times 175\ \mathrm{J/mol}$
$\Rightarrow \Delta G^\circ_{rxn} = 55000 - 52150$
$\Rightarrow \Delta G^\circ_{rxn} = 2850\ \mathrm{J/mol}$
